passages.¶1: Looking for a house for almost a year. Many houses stay a looooong time; some gone in usually 1-2 days. Cast: N is my realtor; J is seller's realtor; C is J's partner; L is J and C's assistant.
passages.¶10: Saturday morning nothing happens; buyer suspects offer kept open to compete with today offers and advertise an offer exists. Asks disclosure of other offer. Saturday afternoon takes a nap; emotionally moved on. Naps once every few years when a big load lifts.
passages.¶11: Saturday 5pm: told another offer will be considered in an hour, submit in time. Buyer suspects no new offer came, his is better, they want a rewrite to pit against other. Drops offer 20K from asking, removes most sweets. N strongly advises against; buyer proceeds.
passages.¶12: Saturday 6pm new offer open until 8:30pm. 7pm: C asks N to fix the price drop, says counteroffer possible. J's name replaced by C on REW; removed from all 4 listings. Meanwhile J busy showing a $3.5M house.
passages.¶13: Saturday 9pm: receives multiple-offers disclosure plus counteroffer 5K above asking, response by 11pm. Buyer reads it as defending forward to recoup 20K. N thinks other offer may really be there with a disliked condition. Extended to morning.
passages.¶14: Saturday 9:30pm N calls: thinks buyer did the right thing and thanks him.
passages.¶15: Sunday 8am: revise to 10K below asking, remove every sweet, respond by 11am. 3 more showings today. Believes they could get 45K below and compete up to 30K below, almost certain nothing above that; calls 10K below best and final.
passages.¶16: Sunday 1pm L to N: offer expired; sending a new Sunday-morning offer with under 2 hours is unprofessional, not in clients' interest. L notes 37 years in V. real-estate admin. N replies: Friday full-price offer stalled; team left 2nd and 3rd unwanted offers; tight timeline fits their pace.
passages.¶17: Sunday 9am N to JCL sends best and final offer. Sunday 5:30pm buyer wants in-person presentation only, likely Monday after 5:30 in N's office. 6pm N replies in-person never happens; sellers hire representation; team may accept by initialing a new deadline; offers resending tonight optionally.
passages.¶18: Sunday 6pm buyer refuses another open offer: sellers had an offer each of past 3 showing days. Monday: thanks N, orders no volunteered competing-offer info and written disclosure letters henceforth. Realtors push 5-10% more to close; buyer won't pay extra 5-10%.
passages.¶19: One week later: bet pays coffee if at/above asking, coffee owed if 10K below or lower. Two weeks later house sold 10K below asking; N buys coffee. First Wednesday house gone for waaay higher than asking.
passages.¶2: Wednesday afternoon: puts highest affordable price on a liked house, still about 30K below asking. Thinks house worth more than offer; hopes for a chance.
passages.¶20: Final thoughts: 7 months ago resisted repeated pushes to go 5-10% more on another house; it sold 5% over buyer price after 7 months. Seller is a marketing/sales person teaching car dealerships to sell.
passages.¶21: System critique: realtors built a system buyers/sellers must obey, playing us as pawns; buyer admits exaggerating. Society negotiates phone holders to houses yet avoids fixing processes.
passages.¶22: Claude debrief: February 2025 residential house, 3-day Friday-Sunday negotiation, walked away. First offer full asking with sweets to avoid bidding war. Pivots: Friday extension, Saturday 20K cut, Sunday 10K-below minimal offer, strict timelines.
passages.¶23: Debrief tactics and lessons: requested written competing-offer disclosure, limited sharing, short windows, stripped sweets, avoided bidding war. Lessons: competing-offer narratives manipulate; demand documentation; detachment advantages; asymmetry mitigated by questioning.
passages.¶24: Debrief verdict: successes were bluff detection, price discipline, learning system; failures no purchase and strained relations; time pressure and price cuts situational. Keep discipline and verification; modify timelines, style, relationships; add metrics and walkaway thresholds.
passages.¶3: Thursday noon sends other houses for weekend showings. Thursday 5pm new house comes on market, added to weekend tour. Thursday 7pm asks N to book last house ASAP Friday.
passages.¶4: Thursday 6pm: first offer not accepted; sellers move forward with other offers. Buyer accepts limits, will move faster; new house very exciting.
passages.¶5: Friday 1pm: likes house, will offer asking price. Wants sweet terms for instant acceptance before rival showings. N advises 10K below to allow negotiation; buyer unconvinced asking price needs negotiating.
passages.¶6: Friday 6pm: offer sent at asking with maximum sweets, deadline same-day midnight. Other showings happened today but an asking-price rival unlikely; good chance.
passages.¶7: Friday 9pm N can't reach seller realtor, keeps trying. N finds silence a bit unprofessional but understands busyness.
passages.¶8: Friday 10:30pm: seller realtor driving up island, busy; asks extension to tomorrow midnight; mentions another offer in passing. Buyer doubts offer, fears bid-war leverage. 4 more showings tomorrow; fears competing offer while waiting.
passages.¶9: Friday 11pm: extends offer to 10:30am Saturday. Reasons morning suffices to accept an offer meeting all conditions.

nodes.text: Buyer chronicles a failed asking-price negotiation, retaliatory cuts, walkaway, and lessons on realtor leverage.
Year-long search in a split market with N, J, C, and L.
Many houses linger very long; some vanish in 1-2 days.
N buyer's realtor; J seller's realtor; C partner; L assistant.
First Wednesday offer at affordability ceiling still fails.
Highest affordable bid sits about 30K below asking price.
Thursday 6pm rejection; sellers proceed with other offers.
Friday asking-price bid seeks instant acceptance before rivals.
Friday 1pm showing convinces; sweet asking-price offer planned.
N advises 10K below to leave negotiation room; buyer unconvinced.
Friday 6pm offer at asking with sweets, deadline midnight same day.
Seller side cites busyness, seeks extension, mentions rival offer.
Friday 10:30pm: driving up island; extend to tomorrow midnight; another offer mentioned.
Buyer doubts the rival offer and fears bid-war leverage.
Friday 11pm counter: extension only to 10:30am Saturday.
Buyer retaliates with cuts; sellers counter above asking.
Saturday 5pm: buyer drops 20K from asking, strips sweets, defying N.
J replaced by C on REW, gone from 4 listings; $3.5M showing noted.
Saturday 9pm counter 5K above asking with disclosure; reply by 11pm.
Saturday silence, rare nap as load lifts; N later endorses cuts.
Sunday email fight ends cooperation; buyer demands in-person terms.
L calls sub-2-hour Sunday deadline unprofessional; cites 37 years admin experience.
N replies Friday full-price stall left unwanted 2nd and 3rd offers.
Sunday 8am: 10K below asking, no sweets, 11am deadline; believes rival ceiling is 45K-30K below.
Buyer refuses further open offers; wants in-person Monday after 5:30.
House sells below asking; buyer sets disclosure rules.
Two weeks later sold 10K below asking; N owes coffee.
New rule: no volunteered offer talk; written disclosure letters required.
Earlier house resisted 5-10% push; sold 5% over bid after 7 months.
Seller trains car dealerships; realtor system plays clients as pawns.
Claude debrief: February 2025, 3-day Friday-Sunday talks, walked away.
Arc: optimistic start, skeptical middle, detached strategic end.
Tactics: disclosure demands, short windows, stripped sweets, no bidding war.
Successes: bluff detection, discipline; failures: no purchase, strained ties.
Keep verification; soften timelines and style; add walkaway thresholds.
